questions.question: Normally in the standing position the center of gravity lies:

options.A: 5 cms anterior to second sacral vertebra
options.B: 5 cms posterior to second sacral vertebra
options.D: 5 cms anterior to second lumbar vertebra

questions.explanation: In standing the centre of gravity lies about 5 cm anterior to the second sacral vertebra.

questions.question: The ligaments of the hip are very weak: Biomechanics 59
questions.explanation: The hip capsule is weakest posteriorly.

questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure and Function/Norkin/3rd Ed./Pg. 298

questions.question: A child with upper leg swelling with pulmonary nodule most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: A child with a swollen thigh and pulmonary nodules most likely has osteosarcoma with lung metastases.

questions.question: Patella tracking dysfunction is a common problem in orthopedics. Dynamic factors for patella tracking dysfunction include:

options.A: Increase in the angulation between the quadriceps muscle and the patella tendon
options.B: A lateral femoral condyle that is not sufficiently prominent anteriorly

questions.explanation: Vastus medialis obliquus insufficiency is a dynamic cause of poor patellar tracking.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Therapeutic Exercise/Kisner/5th Ed./ Pg. 691,697/711
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: When an ultrasonic beam is applied to a cell membrane, it causes unidirectional flow of tissue components. This is termed as:
questions.explanation: Unidirectional fluid flow along a cell membrane is acoustic streaming.

questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Agent in Rehabilitation/Cameron/2nd Ed./Pg. 191

questions.question: The commonest cause of upper GI bleeding is:
questions.explanation: Endoscopy is the investigation.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Aggression resulting from frustration is described by the:
questions.explanation: Dollard and Miller (1939).

questions.question: Pilocarpine is used in the treatment of:
questions.explanation: A muscarinic agonist that causes miosis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: A patient rehabilitating from a spinal cord injury works on self-range of motion activities in sitting. Suddenly, the patient begins to demonstrate signs and symptoms of autonomic dysreflexia. The most appropriate therapist action is to:

options.A: Keep the patient in sitting, monitor blood pressure, and check the bowel and bladder for impairment
options.B: Lie the patient flat, monitor blood pressure, and check the bowel and bladder for impairment
options.C: Lie the patient flat, monitor blood pressure, and give the patient fluids
options.D: Keep the patient sitting, monitor blood pressure, wait for medical assistance

questions.explanation: Keep the patient sitting to lower blood pressure, check bladder and bowel, and monitor BP.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Maximum weight used for skin traction is:
questions.explanation: Skin traction is limited to about 5 kg.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Fever and rigors during blood transfusion should prompt:

options.C: Stopping the transfusion and urgent medical review

questions.explanation: Check for incompatibility.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: While palpating the wrist and hand, it should become apparent that the hamate articulates with the ________ metacarpal?
questions.explanation: The hamate articulates with the fourth (and fifth) metacarpal.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Ulnar deviation of the wrist is performed by:

options.A: Flexor carpi ulnaris and extensor carpi ulnaris

questions.explanation: Radial deviation: FCR, ECRL, ECRB, APL.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham; Norkin & Levangie, Joint Structure and Function (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A therapist records a manual muscle test grade of poor for right hip adduction. The most appropriate patient position to conduct the test would be:
questions.explanation: Grade 2 hip adduction is tested supine with gravity eliminated.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Microwaves are more absorbed in tissues with:
questions.explanation: Microwaves are absorbed more by tissue with high water content.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Intrauterine growth restriction is defined as fetal weight below the:
questions.explanation: Doppler studies assess placental function.

questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Treatment in the early stage of myositis ossifican is:
questions.explanation: Early myositis ossificans is treated by immobilisation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A phase IV cardiac rehabilitation program can best be described as:

options.A: A program of maintenance designed to allow the patient to continue a lifelong routine of exercise and education
options.B: A program that is monitored by electrocardiogram to determine the patient's maximal heart rate and exercise tolerance
options.C: A program that allows for independent progression of exercise at home
options.D: A two to four month program based solely on exercise which allows the patient to attain the appropriate maximal heart rate for his/her age group

questions.explanation: Phase IV is the long-term maintenance phase.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The screening test for HIV is:
questions.explanation: Western blot or NAT is confirmatory.

questions.question: A 55-year-old female diagnosed with a right hip intertrochanteric fracture is eight weeks status postopen reduction and internal fixation with a plate and pinning. The patient has pain with active hip flexion and abduction. Acceptable modalities for this patient would include all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Shortwave diathermy is avoided over metal implants such as a plate and pins.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Agent in Rehabilitation/Cameron/2nd Ed./Pg. 394
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: A therapist develops exercise guidelines for a pregnant woman. Which of the following guideline is not accurate?

options.A: Deep flexion and extension of joints should be avoided
options.B: Heart rate should be measured at times of peak activity
options.C: Duration of exercise should be influenced by perceived exertion
options.D: Fluid intake should be limited before and after exercise

questions.explanation: Fluid intake should be encouraged, not limited, around exercise in pregnancy.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Peripheral nerves can withstand ischemia up to:
questions.explanation: Peripheral nerves tolerate ischaemia for about one hour before conduction fails.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A therapist performs manual muscle test on a patient with unilateral upper extremity weakness. The patient is able to complete 75% of the available range of motion with gravity eliminated. The therapist should record the muscle grade as:
questions.explanation: Moving through 75% of range gravity-eliminated is grade 2 minus (poor minus).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Infected wounds are treated by application of the following dose of UVR:
questions.explanation: Infected wounds are treated with an E4 dose.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Presence of muscle fibrillation indicates which of the following?
questions.explanation: Fibrillation indicates loss of muscle innervation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A patient scheduled for total hip replacement surgery is referred to physical therapy for preoperative instruction. All of the following should be incorporated into the preoperative session except:

options.B: Gait training with an appropriate assistive device
options.C: Basic precautions for early bed mobility
options.D: Proper use of an adduction pillow

questions.explanation: An adduction pillow is used after surgery, not taught pre-operatively in the same way; the other items are standard pre-op teaching.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 205
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A patient with a full-thickness burn receives a skin graft. Immediately after the procedure the graft site requires:

options.B: Long term immobilization of one month

questions.explanation: The graft site is temporarily immobilised to allow graft take.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Thickening of skin following UVR is due to:
questions.explanation: UV thickens the epidermis through stimulation of keratinocytes.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: While examining a patient diagnosed with Achilles tendonitis, a therapist, notes that the foot appears to be pronated in standing. Which motions combine to create pronation?
questions.explanation: Pronation combines abduction, dorsiflexion and eversion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: A therapist orders a wheelchair for a patient with T8-T9 paraplegia. Which wheelchair option is not usually necessary for a patient with paraplegia?
questions.explanation: Handrim projections are not usually needed in paraplegia.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A patient is referred to physical therapy with a C6 nerve root injury. Which of the following clinical findings would not be expected with this type of injury?

options.A: Diminished sensation on the anterior arm and the index finger
options.B: Weakness in the biceps and supinator
options.D: Paresthesias of the long and ring fingers

questions.explanation: C6 root lesions affect thumb and index sensation; paraesthesia of the middle and ring fingers is C7-C8.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Most useful modality for rehabilitation in cervical spine injury with quadriplegia is:
questions.explanation: A tilt table helps adapt to the upright posture after cervical cord injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Acute relapse of multiple sclerosis is treated with:
questions.explanation: Shortens the relapse.

questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The amount of heat delivered to the body by moist hot pack is more than PWB, because:

options.A: The specific heat of water is more than wax
options.B: The specific heat of wax is more than convection
options.C: Moist heat produces heat in body by convection

questions.explanation: Moist packs deliver more heat because the specific heat of water exceeds that of wax.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-probability sampling method?

questions.question: Disease surveillance is the:

options.A: Continuous systematic collection, analysis and interpretation of health data for action

questions.question: In congenital dislocation of knee deformity seen is:

questions.question: Reliable method of increasing central excitation to stimulate motor units in largest proportion of muscle is by:

options.A: Application of assistance to voluntary movement

questions.question: An order is received to perform chest physical therapy on a patient status postabdominal surgery. A chart review identifies right atelectasis. The most appropriate exercise to teach the patient is:

questions.question: The primary area of the residual limb used for weight bearing in a transtibial prosthesis is the:

questions.question: If the radial nerve is severed above the origin of the triceps muscle, what motion of the elbow joint in impossible?

questions.question: The following statements regarding coupling medium used with ultrasound are true except:

options.A: Transmission of ultrasound by aquasonic gel is 40%
options.B: A gel is an ideal coupling medium
options.C: It helps in the transmission of ultrasound
options.D: To eliminate air between transducer head and the patient

questions.explanation: Aquasonic gel transmits more than 40% of the energy.

questions.question: Haemolytic disease of the newborn occurs when:

options.A: An Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive fetus (second pregnancy onwards)

questions.question: A therapist hypothesizes that patient's persistent shoulder pain is caused by an injury to a specific upper extremity muscle. What selective tissue tension assessment would provide the therapist with the most useful information to test the hypothesis?

options.A: Implement a low level exercise program
options.B: Implement breathing exercises and postural drainage technique
options.D: Complete a manual muscle test of the upper and lower extremities

questions.explanation: Breathing exercises and postural drainage address cyanosis and shallow breathing first.

questions.question: Reaching the hand overhead requires:

questions.explanation: Combined movement of the shoulder complex.

questions.question: A physical therapist use proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation techniques to increase muscular strength. The therapist instructs the patient to actively perform a pattern of hip extension, abduction, and medial rotation. This pattern emphasizes strengthening of the:
questions.explanation: Hip extension, abduction and medial rotation emphasises the gluteal muscles.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Candida albicans commonly causes:

questions.question: A therapist position a patient in preparation for postural drainage activities. Which of the following lung segments would not require the foot of the bed to be elevated?

options.A: Anterior segments of the upper lobes

options.D: Lateral basal segments of the lower lobes

questions.explanation: Anterior segments of the upper lobes drain in supine without elevating the foot of the bed.

questions.question: Normal angle between vertical lines of femur and tibia is:

questions.question: A therapist develops a chart detailing expected functional outcomes for a variety of spinal cord injuries. Which is the highest spinal level at which independent transfers with sliding board would be feasible?

questions.question: A patient with an IV in the antecubital region is treated in physical therapy. The therapist would like to instruct the patient in upper extremity active range of motion exercises, but is concerned about placing excessive pressure on the infusion site. Which of the following exercises would not be indicated?
questions.explanation: Elbow flexion and extension would place pressure on an antecubital IV site.

questions.question: Which finding is characteristic of an upper motor neurone lesion?

questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A therapist prepares to treat a patient with limited ankle range of motion using joint mobilization techniques. If the therapist elects to mobilize the talocrural joint in the resting position, the therapist should position the ankle in:

options.C: 10 degrees plantar flexion, midway between inversion and eversion

questions.explanation: The ankle resting position is about 10 degrees plantar flexion, midway between inversion and eversion.

questions.question: An IQ of 50–69 corresponds to:
questions.explanation: Moderate 35–49; severe 20–34; profound below 20.

questions.question: Sudeck's atrophy is another name for:

questions.explanation: Pain, swelling, osteopenia and trophic changes.

questions.question: A patient status postspinal fusion is referred for chest physical therapy. The therapist instructs patient in diaphragmatic breathing exercises. options.A: Direct air so that the nondominant hand rises during inspiration

questions.question: The proportion of solid wax to mineral oil in Paraffin wax treatments should be:

questions.question: A patient is referred to physical therapy diagnosed with right hip trochanteric bursitis. Which clinical finding is usually not associated with trochanteric bursitis?
